page: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the average category. Conversely, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the weak tier. Memory bandwidth tests also register in the bottom 25 percent, although the Passmark memory score achieves an average rating. For specialized workloads, static web serving throughput reaches an average of 6.66 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations perform at 3.99 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-4s_v5 offers high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive multi-threaded CPU processing. However, the tradeoff is lower multi-core performance and memory bandwidth per unit of memory. This profile makes the server appropriate for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications with high RAM requirements but moderate parallel processing needs.
